revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Missing Parentheses?
revealWordProblem.text:
Akela's math teacher gives him a challenge: see how many different values the expression on the board can have, depending on where one set of parentheses is placed. The expression is 48 ÷ 2³ × ½ + 1.7.
Question: How many different values can you come up with? Show the placement that gives each value.
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A chalkboard showing the expression 48 divided by 2 cubed, times one-half, plus 1.7.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Evaluate the original first, following the order of operations: 2³ = 8, then 48 ÷ 8 = 6, then 6 × ½ = 3, then 3 + 1.7 = 4.7. Now try one set of parentheses in each sensible place and evaluate again — for example (48 ÷ 2³) × ½ + 1.7 = 4.7 (no change, because that is already the order), 48 ÷ (2³ × ½) + 1.7 = 48 ÷ 4 + 1.7 = 13.7, and 48 ÷ 2³ × (½ + 1.7) = 6 × 2.2 = 13.2. Each placement that changes which operation happens first gives a new value; a placement that only repeats the existing order gives 4.7 again. Record every distinct result and count them.

vocabulary.definition: A math phrase built from numbers and operations, with no equal sign and no variable.

conceptIntro.heading: Write and Evaluate Numerical Expressions with Exponents
conceptIntro.intro: Grouping symbols change the order of operations. Use parentheses to show which part to find first.
conceptIntro.introEs: Los símbolos de agrupación cambian el orden de las operaciones. Usa paréntesis para mostrar qué parte se halla primero.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Parentheses come first, then powers, then multiply and divide, then add and subtract, so where you put parentheses can change the value.
conceptIntro.keyIdeaEs: Los paréntesis van primero, luego las potencias, luego multiplicar y dividir, y luego sumar y restar, así que dónde pones los paréntesis puede cambiar el valor.

iDo.title: Example · Split a bill
lines: Seven friends split a bill. They order 4 pizzas at 3² dollars each, plus a $6 delivery fee. Write one expression for each friend's share. Evaluate it.
Put the total in parentheses. Then divide by 7: (4 × 3² + 6) ÷ 7
Work inside the parentheses. Then divide: (36 + 6) ÷ 7 = 42 ÷ 7 = 6
linesEs: Siete amigos dividen una cuenta. Piden 4 pizzas a 3² dólares cada una, más $6 de envío. Escribe una expresión para la parte de cada amigo. Evalúala.
Pon el total entre paréntesis. Luego divide entre 7: (4 × 3² + 6) ÷ 7
Trabaja dentro de los paréntesis. Luego divide: (36 + 6) ÷ 7 = 42 ÷ 7 = 6

weDo.title: Try it together — then prove it
lines: Each student ticket costs 2³ dollars. Evaluate 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2³.
Find the power. Then do each multiplication. (2³ is 8 → 30 + 80 + 64)
Why must you find 2³ before you multiply by 8? (The exponent belongs only to the 2. So 8 × 2³ means 8 × 8 = 64, not 8 × 2 × 3.)
linesEs: Cada boleto de estudiante cuesta 2³ dólares. Evalúa 2 × 15 + 4 × 20 + 8 × 2³.
Halla la potencia. Luego haz cada multiplicación. (2³ es 8 → 30 + 80 + 64)
¿Por qué debes hallar 2³ antes de multiplicar por 8? (El exponente es solo del 2. Así que 8 × 2³ significa 8 × 8 = 64, no 8 × 2 × 3.)

together.answer: 2 × 4² + 4 ÷ 4 = 32 + 1 = 33. The parentheses change the order, so they change the value.

onMyOwn.problem: A number is squared. The result is multiplied by 2. Then 5 is added. The final value is 37. What is the number?

onMyOwn.modelExplanation: I undid the steps in reverse order. 37 − 5 = 32, then 32 ÷ 2 = 16. 16 is 4², so the number is 4. Check: 2 × 4² + 5 = 37.
onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: Deshice los pasos en orden inverso. 37 − 5 = 32, luego 32 ÷ 2 = 16. 16 es 4², así que el número es 4. Comprueba: 2 × 4² + 5 = 37.

onMyOwn.modelExplanationEs: Jay multiplicó antes de hallar la potencia. El exponente le pertenece solo al 3, así que primero 3² = 9 y luego 4 × 9 = 36. Su forma solo sirve para (4 × 3)².

onLevel.title: Find the error
onLevel.correctWork: Step 1 multiplies the base by the exponent. A power is repeated multiplication: 3² = 3 × 3 = 9, so the expression evaluates to 20 − 9 = 11.
onLevel.explanation: Step 2's arithmetic is fine — the error is entirely in what 3² means. Reading an exponent as a multiplier is the most common power mistake.

onLevel.explanationEs: La aritmética del Paso 2 está bien — el error está por completo en lo que significa 3². Leer un exponente como un multiplicador es el error más común con las potencias.

onLevel.stem: Seven friends split the bill for a pizza party. They order 4 pizzas at 3² dollars each, plus a one-time $6 delivery fee. Write ONE numerical expression for what each friend owes, evaluate it, and explain why the grouping symbols matter.
onLevel.sampleAnswer: Each friend owes (4 × 3² + 6) ÷ 7. Evaluating: the power first, 3² = 9; then multiply, 4 × 9 = 36; then add inside the grouping symbols, 36 + 6 = 42; then divide, 42 ÷ 7 = $6 each. The grouping symbols matter because without them the expression would read 4 × 3² + 6 ÷ 7, which divides only the delivery fee among the friends and leaves each of them paying for all four pizzas — about $36.86 instead of $6. The parentheses are what say "split the WHOLE bill."

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake with powers is multiplying the base by the exponent: reading 3² as 3 × 2 = 6 instead of 3 × 3 = 9. A second is evaluating strictly left to right, so 3 + 4 × 2 becomes 14 instead of 11. The order of operations exists so one expression has exactly one value: grouping symbols, then powers, then × and ÷ left to right, then + and − left to right.

connect.scenario: A rideshare app charges $2.50 plus $1.75 per mile. The expression for the fare is 2.50 + 1.75m, where m is miles traveled. Your friend lives 8 miles away.
connect.promptQuestion: How much will the ride cost? How does the expression model this situation?
connect.prompt: The ride costs $___ because 2.50 + 1.75(___) = ___. The 2.50 is the ___ and 1.75 is the ___.

choices: A flat base fee charged no matter how far you go
check.explanation: 2.50 has no variable attached, so it is the constant — the flat fee you pay on any ride.
check.explanationEs: 2.50 no tiene ninguna variable pegada, así que es la constante — la cuota fija que pagas en cualquier viaje.
choicesEs: Una cuota base fija que se cobra sin importar qué tan lejos vayas

choices: The cost per mile, multiplied by the number of miles
check.explanation: 1.75 is the coefficient of m, so it is the rate: $1.75 for every mile traveled.
check.explanationEs: 1.75 es el coeficiente de m, así que es la tasa: $1.75 por cada milla recorrida.
choicesEs: El costo por milla, multiplicado por el número de millas

connect.modelAnswer: Substitute m = 8: 2.50 + 1.75(8) = 2.50 + 14 = $16.50. The 2.50 is the constant base fee charged on every ride, and the 1.75 is the coefficient — the rate charged per mile.
connect.promptEs: El viaje cuesta $___ porque 2.50 + 1.75(___) = ___. El 2.50 es la ___ y 1.75 es la ___.
connect.scenarioEs: Una app de viajes cobra $2.50 más $1.75 por milla. La expresión de la tarifa es 2.50 + 1.75m, donde m son las millas recorridas. Tu amigo vive a 8 millas.
connect.promptQuestionEs: ¿Cuánto costará el viaje? ¿Cómo modela la expresión esta situación?
connect.modelAnswerEs: Sustituye m = 8: 2.50 + 1.75(8) = 2.50 + 14 = $16.50. El 2.50 es la cuota base constante que se cobra en cada viaje, y el 1.75 es el coeficiente — la tasa que se cobra por milla.

exitTicket.explanation: Powers first: 2³ = 8. Then multiply left to right: 2 × 15 = 30 and 8 × 8 = 64. Then add: 30 + 64 = 94.
choiceFeedback: That treats 2³ as 2 × 3 = 6, giving 30 + 48 + 46. An exponent means repeated multiplication, not multiplication by the exponent.
That leaves the power unevaluated: 30 + 8 × 15 is not the expression given.
That adds before multiplying: (2 × 15 + 8) × 8. Multiplication comes before addition.
hints: What must be evaluated before any multiplying?
2³ means 2 × 2 × 2.
After the power, multiply left to right, then add.
exitTicket.explanationEs: Primero las potencias: 2³ = 8. Luego multiplica de izquierda a derecha: 2 × 15 = 30 y 8 × 8 = 64. Luego suma: 30 + 64 = 94.
choiceFeedbackEs: Eso trata 2³ como 2 × 3 = 6, dando 30 + 48 + 46. Un exponente significa multiplicación repetida, no multiplicar por el exponente.
Eso deja la potencia sin evaluar: 30 + 8 × 15 no es la expresión dada.
Eso suma antes de multiplicar: (2 × 15 + 8) × 8. La multiplicación va antes que la suma.
hintsEs: ¿Qué se debe evaluar antes de cualquier multiplicación?

Después de la potencia, multiplica de izquierda a derecha y luego suma.

questions.stem: In 2⁵, which number is the base and which is the exponent?
questions.explanation: The base is the number being multiplied (2) and the exponent tells how many times (5).
choiceFeedback: This uses the same number for both spots. The raised number is a different value from the one written on the line.
This swaps the two numbers. The base is the number being multiplied over and over; the exponent is the small raised number.
This uses the raised number for both spots. The number written on the line is the base, and it is different from the exponent.
choiceFeedbackEs: Esto usa el mismo número en los dos lugares. El número elevado es un valor distinto del que está escrito en la línea.
Esto intercambia los dos números. La base es el número que se multiplica una y otra vez; el exponente es el número pequeño elevado.
Esto usa el número elevado en los dos lugares. El número escrito en la línea es la base, y es distinto del exponente.
questions.stemEs: En 2⁵, ¿cuál número es la base y cuál es el exponente?
questions.explanationEs: La base es el número que se multiplica (2) y el exponente dice cuántas veces (5).

questions.stem: Which expression shows 5³ as repeated multiplication?
questions.explanation: The exponent 3 means the base 5 is used as a factor three times.
choiceFeedback: This repeats the exponent as a factor. The exponent only tells you how many times to write the base.
This multiplies 5 by 3 in one step instead of writing 5 as a factor three separate times.
This is repeated addition, which is what multiplication looks like — an exponent means repeated multiplication instead.
choiceFeedbackEs: Esto repite el exponente como factor. El exponente solo te dice cuántas veces escribir la base.
Esto multiplica 5 por 3 en un solo paso en vez de escribir el 5 como factor tres veces por separado.
Esto es una suma repetida, que es lo que representa una multiplicación — un exponente significa multiplicación repetida.
questions.explanationEs: El exponente 3 significa que la base 5 se usa como factor tres veces.
